name: Siliguri (NJP and Bagdogra)
tagline: Arrive at NJP or Bagdogra, then find the right jeep
meta_description: Siliguri arrival guide: where shared jeeps leave for Darjeeling, Gangtok, Kalimpong and Mirik, prepaid taxis, fares, one-night stays and food near NJP.
summary: Siliguri is the gateway for Darjeeling, Sikkim, Bhutan and the Dooars. Bagdogra Airport (IXB) is 14 km out, NJP station 6 km. Shared jeeps leave from NJP and the Tenzing Norgay terminus on Hill Cart Road between about 7 a.m. and 3 p.m.; after that, take a prepaid or reserved car or stay one night.
intro: Almost everyone who visits the eastern Himalaya passes through Siliguri, and almost nobody plans for it. That is how people end up paying ₹5,000 for a car they could have shared for ₹350, or arriving at a jeep stand at 4 p.m. to find it empty. This page is the practical fix. Siliguri is a flat, busy trading city of about 700,000 people on the Mahananda river, spread across Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri districts. It is not pretty, but it works: one airport, two big railway stations, a state bus terminus, a Sikkim bus terminus and several jeep stands, all within 15 km.

The three arrival points are New Jalpaiguri (NJP), the main railway station in the south of the city; Bagdogra Airport (IXB), about 14 km west of the centre; and the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road, next to Siliguri Junction station, where state buses arrive. Hill Cart Road is the spine of the city: it runs north from near NJP past the bus terminus and Pradhan Nagar to Darjeeling More and on into the hills. Sevoke Road branches north-east towards Sevoke, the Teesta, Kalimpong, Gangtok and the Dooars.

Our rule of thumb is simple. If you land before 1 p.m., go straight up by shared jeep or reserved car. If you land after 2 p.m., do not race the dark up a mountain road: book a room near NJP or on Hill Cart Road, eat well, and leave at 7 a.m. when the stands are full of jeeps and the light is good. A night here costs ₹1,200–2,500 in a decent budget hotel, much less than a rushed evening drive and a late check-in in Darjeeling or Gangtok.

story.title: A railway town that moved to NJP
paras: Siliguri grew as a railhead. When the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway opened in 1880–81, its southern terminus was Siliguri Town station, where passengers from Calcutta changed from the main line to the little two-foot-gauge trains for the hills. Tea chests came down and rice, kerosene and mail went up. Merchants from Bihar, Rajasthan and Bengal set up shop along Hill Cart Road, and the town became the market for the hills, the Dooars and Nepal's eastern plains.

Partition in 1947 changed everything. With East Pakistan to the south and Nepal to the west, the only land link between the rest of India and the north-east became a strip roughly 20–22 km wide at its narrowest, now called the Siliguri Corridor. A new broad-gauge station, New Jalpaiguri, opened in 1960, and in 1964 the toy train line was extended south to meet it. Today NJP is the busiest station in the region and Siliguri is the place where roads, rail and an airport all meet.
story.source: Wikipedia 'Siliguri' and 'Darjeeling Himalayan Railway'; UNESCO listing of the Mountain Railways of India (1999)

did_you_know: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway originally started at Siliguri Town station in 1880–81 and was extended south to New Jalpaiguri only in 1964.
Local historian Sailen Debnath explains the name Siliguri as 'a stack of pebbles or stones', a fit for a city on the Mahananda's stony bed.
The Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus, opened in 1984, is named after the Everest climber who made his home in Darjeeling.

highlights.title: Shared jeeps for every hill town
highlights.text: Jeeps for Darjeeling leave from the NJP forecourt and the stand by the Tenzing Norgay terminus; Gangtok jeeps leave from NJP and the SNT terminus; Kalimpong jeeps from the Hill Cart Road and Sevoke Road stands. Most leave between 7 a.m. and 3 p.m., when full.

highlights.title: Prepaid taxi counters
highlights.text: Bagdogra has a prepaid taxi counter next to the arrival-hall exit and NJP has one opposite the station entrance, open in daytime. Rates are fixed per vehicle, which protects you from haggling after a long journey.

highlights.title: The toy train from NJP
highlights.text: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway's long run from NJP to Darjeeling takes about seven hours across 88 km, through Sukna, Rangtong, Tindharia and Kurseong. It is a full-day experience rather than transport, and seats are booked on IRCTC.

highlights.title: A good last night near the airport
highlights.text: If your flight leaves before noon, sleep in Siliguri rather than leaving Darjeeling or Gangtok at 4 a.m. Landslides and fog can close mountain roads without warning, and a night on the plains costs less than a missed flight.

highlights.title: Momos, thali and Hong Kong Market
highlights.text: Siliguri eats well and cheaply: steamed momos and thukpa in small Tibetan and Nepali kitchens, Bengali fish thalis, Bihari litti and Marwari sweets. Hong Kong Market, off Hill Cart Road, sells everything from jackets to phone covers.

highlights.title: Salugara and the Coronation Bridge
highlights.text: If you have a spare half-day, the 100-foot stupa at Salugara Monastery is 6 km out on Sevoke Road, and the 1941 Coronation Bridge over the Teesta is 22 km beyond the city.

how_to_reach.text: Bagdogra Airport (IXB) has direct flights from Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Guwahati and others; routes change by season. The prepaid taxi counter is next to the arrival exit. A car to the city centre or NJP costs ₹400–700, indicative 2026. There are no shared jeeps to the hills from the airport itself, so either reserve a car or go to Siliguri first.

New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is on the main line to Guwahati, with overnight trains from Kolkata such as the Darjeeling Mail and Padatik Express, the daytime Vande Bharat from Howrah, and long-distance trains from Delhi. Siliguri Junction, next to the bus terminus, serves trains on the Dooars line towards New Mal, Hasimara and Alipurduar, including the Kanchankanya Express from Sealdah.

The Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road is the hub for state (NBSTC) and private buses to Kolkata, Malbazar, Alipurduar, Cooch Behar and further. Buses run to Phuentsholing in Bhutan and Kathmandu in Nepal. The Sikkim Nationalised Transport (SNT) terminus for Gangtok buses is a three-minute walk up the same road.

Shared jeeps (Sumo, Bolero, Max, about 10 seats) come down from Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Gangtok and Mirik to NJP and Hill Cart Road all day, and leave again for the hills when full. The two front seats next to the driver are the most comfortable; you can book them, or the whole back row, by paying for every seat.

where_to_stay: Stay near where you leave from. For an early train or a jeep from NJP, the station approach and Hill Cart Road south have dozens of budget hotels at ₹1,200–2,500; check the room before paying, as quality varies. Pradhan Nagar and the Hill Cart Road stretch near the Tenzing Norgay terminus suit jeep and bus departures; the WBTDC's Mainak Tourism Property and Sinclairs Siliguri are here, and Courtyard by Marriott is at Mallaguri. For a quiet night before an early flight, Mayfair Tea Resort sits in a tea garden between the city and Bagdogra.
costs: Shared jeep NJP or Siliguri → Darjeeling
Reserved car NJP or IXB → Gangtok
Prepaid car Bagdogra → Siliguri or NJP
budget_tip: Take a shared auto or city bus from the airport gate to Hill Cart Road (₹30–80) and board a shared jeep there, instead of paying ₹3,500 or more for a reserved car from the airport.
tips: Be at the jeep stand by 8 a.m.; after 2 p.m. jeeps to Gangtok and Kalimpong thin out, and after 3 p.m. you may wait an hour or not find one at all.
Agree on the fare per seat before luggage goes on the roof, and keep valuables in your lap rather than in the roof carrier.

Foreign nationals going to Sikkim can get the Sikkim Inner Line Permit at the Rangpo border check post or through Sikkim Tourism; carry passport copies and photos, and check current status before you travel.
Check the status of NH10 before heading to Gangtok or Kalimpong; since the 2023 Teesta flood the road has had long closures, with traffic diverted via Lava or other routes.
Use the official prepaid counters or a known app-booked cab; touts inside the NJP concourse often quote double.

experiences.title: Toy train from NJP into the hills
experiences.cost: ₹1,400–1,600 a seat in first or AC chair class, indicative
experiences.image_query: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway Sukna toy train
experiences.summary: The full run of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway starts at NJP in the plains and climbs 88 km to Darjeeling through loops and zig-zags. It is slow, about seven hours, and best treated as a day out rather than the fastest way up.
body: The UNESCO-listed Darjeeling Himalayan Railway runs from New Jalpaiguri at about 100 m to Darjeeling at roughly 2,200 m. The scheduled through train leaves NJP in the morning, crosses Siliguri, and starts climbing after Sukna, where the forest of the Mahananda sanctuary closes in. Above Rangtong come the loops and zig-zag reversals that let the train gain height on a mountainside too steep for an ordinary railway.

Most of the line runs alongside or across Hill Cart Road, so you see the shops, school children and tea stalls of Tindharia, Mahanadi and Kurseong at walking pace. Kurseong is a natural break. Above it the train passes Sonada and Ghum, the highest station on the line at about 2,258 m, before dropping round the Batasia Loop into Darjeeling. Timings change with the season and with landslide repairs, and diesel engines haul most through trains.

Book through IRCTC as soon as your dates are fixed; seats on this train are limited and sell out in October and May. If seven hours is too long, take a jeep up and ride the short joy train from Darjeeling to Ghum instead, or take the steam service from Darjeeling towards Kurseong where it runs. Check current timetables before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does the toy train take from NJP to Darjeeling
faqs.a: About seven to eight hours for the 88 km run, if there are no delays. Jeeps cover the same climb in about three to three and a half hours. That is why most travellers go up by road and ride a shorter section, such as the Darjeeling–Ghum joy ride, by train. Timings change with the season and repairs, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I book the NJP Darjeeling toy train
faqs.a: Seats are sold on IRCTC like any other Indian Railways train, usually up to 60 days ahead under current rules. Search for trains from NJP to DJ. Through trains have a small number of first class and AC chair coaches, and they sell out in Puja, winter and summer holidays. Book as soon as your dates are firm and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the toy train worth it for children
faqs.a: For a whole day, only if they love trains. Most children enjoy two or three hours and then get restless. A good compromise is to ride from NJP or Siliguri to Kurseong, about half the line, and continue by jeep, or take the two-hour joy ride from Darjeeling around the Batasia Loop to Ghum and back.

experiences.title: A first-night food walk on Hill Cart Road
experiences.summary: Siliguri eats from three directions: the hills send momos and thukpa, Bengal sends fish and rice, Bihar and Rajasthan send litti, kachori and sweets. A slow walk between Hill Cart Road, Bidhan Market and Sevoke Road covers all three for a few hundred rupees.
body: Start near the Tenzing Norgay terminus, where small Tibetan and Nepali kitchens sell steamed or fried momos, thukpa and chowmein at ₹60–150 a plate. Ask for the red chilli sauce on the side; it is hotter than it looks. Many of these places close by 9 p.m., so go early, and pick the busy ones with a quick turnover.

For a proper meal, a Bengali 'hotel' near Bidhan Market or along Hill Cart Road will serve rice, dal, a vegetable, fish curry and chutney as a thali for ₹150–300, with river fish such as rohu or bata and, in season, hilsa at a higher price. Marwari sweet shops sell kachori and samosa in the morning and sweets all day, and in the evenings litti-chokha carts appear near the markets.

Finish on Sevoke Road, where newer cafés and bakeries stay open later. Buy a packet of Darjeeling tea here only from a proper shop with sealed, dated packs; the loose 'first flush' in plastic bags at the bus stand is rarely what it claims. If you arrive late and tired, every mid-range hotel on Hill Cart Road has a restaurant, and the Courtyard and Sinclairs serve until late.

faqs.q: What food is Siliguri known for
faqs.a: Siliguri is known for momos and thukpa from the hills, Bengali fish thalis, and the Marwari and Bihari snacks of a trading city: kachori, samosa, litti-chokha and sweets. It is not a fine-dining city, but a good meal costs ₹150–300. In the Dooars beyond, look out for Rajbanshi dishes made with dried fish and greens.

faqs.q: Is street food in Siliguri safe
faqs.a: Busy stalls with high turnover are generally fine; food cooked fresh in front of you is the safest. Drink only bottled or filtered water, skip raw salads at roadside stalls and avoid cut fruit that has been standing in the sun. If you have a sensitive stomach, eat at a sit-down Bengali hotel or your own hotel for the first night.

faqs.q: Where can I eat near NJP station late at night
faqs.a: The station approach and the Hill Cart Road stretch just north of NJP have small hotels and dhabas that serve rice, roti, egg curry and chowmein until about 10 or 11 p.m. Inside the station there are food stalls and a refreshment room. Very late, your best option is a hotel restaurant or ordering in through a food app.

experiences.title: Salugara Monastery and its 100-foot stupa
experiences.best_time: Mornings or late afternoon, all year
experiences.summary: About 6 km from the city centre on Sevoke Road, Salugara Monastery is known for its white stupa, roughly 100 feet tall, set in a quiet garden. It is the easiest calm hour in Siliguri if you are waiting for a train or a late flight.
body: Salugara is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery on the northern edge of the city, on the road to Sevoke. Its tall white stupa, about 100 feet high with a gilded spire, can be seen from Sevoke Road, and the compound around it has prayer wheels and a small temple hall. Walk around the stupa clockwise, as is the custom, and spin the wheels with your right hand.

Visitors are welcome in daylight hours. Dress modestly, take off your shoes before entering any shrine room, and ask before photographing monks or ceremonies. There is no entry fee; a small offering in the donation box is fine if you wish. It is a pleasant place to sit for half an hour in the late afternoon when the light is soft and the traffic noise drops.

Combine it with an evening at ISKCON's large temple on the city's north side, or keep going on Sevoke Road to the Coronation Bridge and the Sevokeshwari Kali temple at Sevoke, 22 km from the city. An auto or app cab from Hill Cart Road to Salugara costs ₹150–300 each way, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: How far is Salugara Monastery from NJP
faqs.a: Roughly 10–12 km, or 30–45 minutes depending on traffic. From the Tenzing Norgay terminus on Hill Cart Road it is about 6–7 km along Sevoke Road. An auto-rickshaw or app cab is the easiest way to go, at about ₹150–300 each way, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee at Salugara Monastery
faqs.a: No. Entry is free in daytime, and donations are optional. Remove your shoes before going into shrine rooms, walk clockwise around the stupa, and ask before taking photos of monks. Visiting hours are informal, so go between about 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. to be safe.

faqs.q: What else can I see in Siliguri in half a day
faqs.a: Combine Salugara Monastery with the ISKCON temple, a walk through Hong Kong Market and Bidhan Market, and a momo stop on Hill Cart Road. If you have a car for four or five hours, go out to Sevoke for the Coronation Bridge, the Kali temple and the Teesta river view, and return before dark.

experiences.title: Hong Kong Market and Bidhan Market
experiences.best_time: Late morning to evening, closed or quiet on some Sundays
experiences.summary: Siliguri is a trading town, and its markets show it. Hong Kong Market off Hill Cart Road is a maze of small shops selling jackets, shoes, bags and electronics, while Bidhan Market next door is the place for vegetables, dried fish, spices and everyday goods.
body: Locals usually explain the name Hong Kong Market by the imported goods it became known for: cheap electronics, watches and synthetic clothes, much of it foreign-made. Today it is a dense block of narrow lanes off Hill Cart Road where you can buy a warm jacket, gloves, a rain poncho or a phone charger before going up to the hills. Prices start high; bargaining is expected, and a third off the first quote is normal.

Bidhan Market, a short walk away, is where Siliguri shops for food. Look for the stalls of dried fish, the river fish laid out in the morning, local greens, betel nut, and bags of Dooars tea sold by weight. It is noisy and crowded, and a good place to see how the plains feed the hills.

Keep your phone and wallet in a front pocket, carry small notes, and avoid buying branded goods that look too cheap. If you need warm clothes for Sandakphu, North Sikkim or a winter morning in an open safari jeep, this is the cheapest place on the route to buy them.

faqs.q: What can I buy at Hong Kong Market Siliguri
faqs.a: Jackets, fleeces, gloves, caps, shoes, bags, rain gear, phone accessories and small electronics, mostly unbranded or imported. It is the cheapest place on the route to buy warm clothes before going up to the hills. Bargain firmly and check zips and seams. Do not expect genuine branded goods at market prices.

faqs.q: Is Hong Kong Market open on Sunday
faqs.a: Many shops open on Sunday but some close or open late, and the market is busiest in the evenings and on Saturdays. Hours vary by shop. If you need something specific before an early jeep, visit the evening before rather than relying on a Sunday morning.

faqs.q: Is it safe to walk around Siliguri markets
faqs.a: Yes, in daytime and early evening. The lanes are crowded, so watch for pickpockets, keep bags in front and carry only the cash you need. The area is lit and busy until about 8 or 9 p.m. Women travelling alone usually find it comfortable, though staring is common in all crowded Indian markets.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps for Darjeeling leave from in Siliguri
faqs.a: From two main places: the forecourt of NJP station, and the jeep stand near the Tenzing Norgay Central Bus Terminus on Hill Cart Road. Jeeps run from about 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. and leave when full, usually 10 passengers. The fare is about ₹300–400 a seat, indicative 2026. The ride takes three to three and a half hours.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps for Gangtok leave from
faqs.a: From NJP station in daytime, and from the Sikkim Nationalised Transport (SNT) terminus on Hill Cart Road, three minutes' walk from the Tenzing Norgay bus terminus. SNT also runs buses. Expect ₹400–550 a seat, indicative 2026, and four to five hours. Jeeps thin out after 2 p.m. There are no shared jeeps from Bagdogra Airport itself.

faqs.q: Where do shared jeeps for Kalimpong and Mirik leave
faqs.a: Kalimpong jeeps leave from the stand near the Tenzing Norgay terminus, from Darjeeling More, and from near Vishal cinema at 2nd Mile on Sevoke Road, mostly before 3 p.m., for about ₹250–350 a seat. Mirik jeeps and buses leave from around the Tenzing Norgay terminus for about ₹200–250. Fares are indicative, 2026.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi from Bagdogra Airport to Darjeeling
faqs.a: A reserved small car from the Bagdogra prepaid counter costs about ₹3,500–4,500 and a larger SUV ₹4,500–5,500, indicative 2026, for a drive of three to three and a half hours. If you are alone or a couple, go into Siliguri by auto or cab first and take a shared jeep for ₹300–400 a seat.

faqs.q: Is there a prepaid taxi at NJP
faqs.a: Yes. The prepaid taxi booth is opposite the main station entrance and works in daytime, from about 7 a.m. Fixed rates cover city drops and hill destinations such as Darjeeling, Gangtok and Kalimpong. Bagdogra Airport also has a prepaid counter next to the arrivals exit. Rates change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Should I stay a night in Siliguri
faqs.a: Stay a night if you arrive after about 2 p.m., if roads to the hills are blocked, or if you have a morning flight or train out. Mountain drives in the dark after a long journey are tiring and riskier. Budget rooms near NJP cost ₹1,200–2,500; comfortable hotels ₹4,500–8,000, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: How far is NJP from Bagdogra Airport
faqs.a: About 15–18 km, or 30–50 minutes depending on traffic. A prepaid or app-booked car costs about ₹500–800, indicative 2026. The Tenzing Norgay bus terminus and Siliguri Junction are in between, about 14 km from the airport and 6 km from NJP.

faqs.q: Can I go from Siliguri to Bhutan by bus
faqs.a: Yes. Buses run from the Tenzing Norgay terminus to Phuentsholing, about 160 km and four to five hours, and many buses also go to Jaigaon, the Indian border town. Indians need a passport or voter ID for the Bhutan entry permit, issued at Phuentsholing, plus the Sustainable Development Fee. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a helicopter from Bagdogra to Gangtok
faqs.a: Sikkim's helicopter service has run between Bagdogra and Gangtok in some seasons, taking about 35 minutes with only a few seats and a tight baggage limit of around 10 kg per person. It is weather dependent and often cancelled in cloud. Treat it as a bonus, not your only plan, and check current status before you travel.
